title: Mastery challenge: preview rises from a live feed

checklist.step: Return the first rises, each with the reading just before it
Read no further than the last rise asked for, and show each step

hints: Which information is needed to decide whether the next reading forms a result?
A rejected pair still changes which reading is immediately before the next one.
Retain the last source value and count completed results; stop before another request once the preview is full.

questions.prompt: What must a returned pair describe?

choices.why: The task concerns adjacent rises, not sorting.
Filtering readings first could create pairs that were never adjacent.
Both readings must be neighbors in the source.

questions.prompt: Which reading is needed when the next one arrives?

choices.why: Adjacency refers to the most recent input, even after a fall or equality.
The first reading is not generally adjacent to later inputs.
A previous maximum can belong far earlier in the source.

questions.prompt: What determines how many source values are needed?

choices.why: Rejected pairs can occur between returned ones.
Demand ends at that rise, or at finite exhaustion if fewer exist.
The magnitude of values does not determine their positions.

questions.prompt: On readings 4, 1, 3, comparing every value with the first reading misses which result?

choices.why: The last value rises from its immediate predecessor, despite being below the first value.
